title: Diffusion and facilitated diffusion; Osmosis and water potential
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MB03a#t1 term and clue written for the game; MB03a#t3 term and clue written for the game; MB03a#t4 term and clue written for the game; MB02a#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MB02a#N.7a, MB02b#N.3, MB03a#N.3a, MB02a#N.12, MB03a#N.6a, MB03a#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Osmosis
items.clue: Net movement of water across a partially permeable membrane.

items.label: Plasmolysis
items.clue: The membrane pulls away from the wall as water leaves a walled cell.

items.label: Turgor pressure
items.clue: Push of the cell contents on the wall after water has entered a walled cell.

items.label: Facilitated diffusion
items.clue: Passive net movement down a concentration gradient through a membrane protein.

questions.stem: A potassium channel in a cell membrane is open. Which statement describes the movement of ions through it?

options.text: Potassium ions diffuse through, down their gradient, with no ATP used.
Potassium ions and any other ions of similar size diffuse through the open pore.
Potassium ions are moved through in whichever direction the cell requires.
Potassium ions are carried through using energy from the hydrolysis of ATP.

questions.explanation: The channel gives one specific ion a hydrophilic route through the hydrophobic core. The ions move by facilitated diffusion, down their gradient, with no ATP.

questions.stem: An exchange surface changes: its surface area becomes 3 times as large, the difference in concentration across it becomes 2 times as large, and its thickness becomes 1.5 times as large. By what factor does the rate of diffusion change?
Two adjacent plant cells have water potentials of −300 kPa (cell A) and −900 kPa (cell B). Which statement describes the net movement of water between them?

options.text: From B to A, because −900 kPa is the larger number, so B has the higher water potential.
There is no net movement, because both water potentials are negative.
From A to B only if the cells use energy to pump it, because water cannot move down a gradient by itself.
From A to B, because water moves from higher to lower water potential.

questions.explanation: −300 kPa is the higher water potential. Water moves from higher to lower water potential, so from A to B, until the two are equal.

questions.stem: A hypothetical toxin binds to and blocks all of the channel and transport proteins in the plasma membrane of a cell. Which prediction about the cell, immediately after exposure to the toxin, is best supported?

options.text: Its uptake of both glucose and O₂ will stop, since all substances cross through proteins.
Its glucose uptake will not change, since glucose passes freely through the phospholipid bilayer.
Its glucose uptake will rise through other routes to meet the cell's own need for glucose.
Its glucose uptake will fall sharply, while O₂ will still diffuse in across the bilayer.

questions.stem: A strip of onion epidermis is mounted in a concentrated sucrose solution and viewed under a microscope. Which statement describes what happens to its cells?

options.text: Water leaves each cell by osmosis and the whole cell, wall included, shrinks and crumples inward, just as an animal cell crenates.
Water leaves each cell by osmosis, the protoplast shrinks and its membrane pulls away from the wall: the cells are plasmolysed.
Water leaves each cell by osmosis and an empty space forms between the wall and the membrane, because the wall lets nothing through.
Water enters each cell by osmosis, because the concentrated solution is hypotonic to them, and the cells become turgid.

questions.stem: Jam contains so much sugar that most bacteria landing on it cannot grow. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Sugar diffuses into the bacteria until there is enough inside them to poison them.
Water leaves the bacteria by osmosis into the jam, so their cytoplasm shrinks and they cannot grow.
Water enters the bacteria from the jam, so the bacteria swell up and burst.
Their cell walls stop any water from crossing, so the bacteria cannot take in water.

questions.explanation: The jam is far more concentrated than the cytoplasm. Water leaves the cells by osmosis; the contents shrink away from the wall, and without water the cells cannot grow.
